title: Incompatible result from TiDB with MySQL
body:
## Bug Report

Please answer these questions before submitting your issue. Thanks!

### 1. Minimal reproduce step (Required)

<!-- a step by step guide for reproducing the bug. -->

```sql
-- Step1: Prepare Data
CREATE TABLE t1 (
  col11 int(16) NOT NULL,
  col12 varchar(255) NOT NULL,
  col13 timestamp NOT NULL,
  PRIMARY KEY (col11, col12, col13)
) ENGINE=InnoDB DEFAULT CHARSET=utf8 COLLATE=utf8_general_ci;

INSERT INTO t1 (col11, col12, col13) VALUES
(212, 'Cindy', '2021-10-29 00:00:00'),
(1104, 'George', '2022-07-27 00:00:00');

ALTER TABLE t1 SET TIFLASH REPLICA 1; 

-- Step2: Execute Query
SELECT /*+ READ_FROM_STORAGE(TIFLASH[t1])*/ 
       MAX(t1.col11) AS r1, MIN(t1.col12) AS r2 FROM t1
WHERE t1.col13 IN ('2021-10-29', '2004-05-14')
GROUP BY t1.col13 HAVING t1.col13 <= '2022-03-24';
-- output:
Empty set (0.06 sec)
```

### 2. What did you expect to see? (Required)

I find that tiflash is incompatible with MySQL 8.4.0 in this query.

### 3. What did you see instead (Required)

```sql
// MySQL
MySQL [test]> SELECT /*+ READ_FROM_STORAGE(TIFLASH[t1])*/
    ->        MAX(t1.col11) AS r1, MIN(t1.col12) AS r2 FROM t1
    -> WHERE t1.col13 IN ('2021-10-29', '2004-05-14')
    -> GROUP BY t1.col13 HAVING t1.col13 <= '2022-03-24';
+------+-------+
| r1   | r2    |
+------+-------+
|  212 | Cindy |
+------+-------+
1 row in set (0.00 sec)
```

### 4. What is your TiDB version? (Required)

<!-- Paste the output of SELECT tidb_version() -->

mysql> select version();
+--------------------+
| version()          |
+--------------------+
| 8.0.11-TiDB-v8.5.0 |
+--------------------+
1 row in set (0.00 sec)

@reporter What I explained above is not to say that this is the expected behavior. I was merely speculating that the issue might be due to the timestamp type involving timezone conversion, which could potentially lead to problems in the implementation that were not properly handled. This is indeed a bug and not the intended behavior. After locating the cause, it will be fixed in a future version.

And as a temporary workaround without upgrading the cluster version, what action can be taken.
